site: Site23, Malapert massif, lunar south pole

averaging.method: block mean of 6 x 6 pixels; a block with any missing pixel would be left missing

methods.slope: central difference: 4 neighbours in a 3x3 window (slope_degrees from terrain.py)
methods.roughness: best-fit plane removed in each window, then population standard deviation of the leftover heights (roughness_detrended from terrain.py)

whole_site.description: whole Site23 map at 30 m, edge pixels skipped

original_5m_slope.note: LOLA's own slope map, not recomputed here; for comparison only

caveats: Slope uncertainty: LOLA's median RMS slope error is about 1.5 to 2.5 degrees. The product page says 'The LDEM height and slope uncertainties within the RoIs are similar across all the sites with a median RMS Z error ~ 0.30 - 0.50 m and a median RMS slope error ~ 1.5 - 2.5°' (https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78). This is a median over the regions of interest of all sites, not a value for each Site23 pixel.

Interpolated heights: about 90 percent of the 5 m pixels are interpolated, not direct LOLA measurements. The product page says 'the fraction of interpolated 5-m pixels in these polar LDEMs is necessarily large (~90%)' (https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78). This is for the polar maps in general; the share for Site23 alone was not computed.
Block means: the 30 m heights are averages of 6 x 6 blocks of 5 m pixels. This smooths the surface and can lower the slope; compare with original_5m_slope.
Different areas: the Moon value covers the whole 21 km x 21 km Site23 map near the south pole (about 85.6 to 86.3 S); the Earth value in terrain.json covers a 10 km x 10 km square.
Projection: map meters are 0.10 to 0.15 percent longer than true ground meters at this site (polar stereographic, true scale at the pole). This was not corrected.

for: slope uncertainty (median RMS slope error ~1.5-2.5 deg)
